source.title: SML: Enhance the Network Smoothness with Skip Meta Logit for CTR Prediction
source.authors: Wenlong Deng; Lang Lang; Z. Liu; B. Liu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares deep plain DNNs with a different skip-path design and reports whether training remains stable as depth increases. It does not use the identity residual shortcuts or classification-error measure in V3.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CTR AUC and logloss comparisons, but those test predictive performance rather than training classification error. The depth result reports training collapse or stability without exact training-error values. No results bear on V1, V2, V4, V5 or V6.
record.test_reason: The study uses skip-connection findings to develop SML and evaluates its CTR performance. It does not test any listed version: its depth experiment uses fully connected networks without batch normalization, different shortcuts, and test-set AUC/logloss rather than training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation of the depth experiment. More fully, they conclude that SML improves CTR-model optimization and expressiveness, yields consistent predictive-performance gains across selected models on two datasets, and improves online business metrics. Their claims of collapse at depth 27 and stability through depth 100 are supported here by reported test-set AUC/logloss, not measured training classification error.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes Skip Logit with Meta Tanh for CTR prediction; it does not reproduce the listed claim's benchmark classification-error recipes or identity-shortcut comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Network depth; vanilla DNN collapses at depth 27, whereas DNN with SML is reported stable up to depth 100.

fits_no_version.finding: On Criteo, the authors report vanilla fully connected DNN training collapse at depth 27 and stable SML training through depth 100, using test-set AUC/logloss curves. Batch normalization is disabled.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SML preserves CTR predictive performance across greater network depths than the tested vanilla fully connected DNN.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.1.2 presents a conditional theorem that critical points of a linear Skip Logit population-risk objective are global minima. It does not study ReLU teacher-student optimization or extra student neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear Skip Logit networks have no nonglobal critical points under the theorem's stated assumptions.

record.problems: The depth comparison is reported on Criteo and uses AUC and logloss curves, not training classification-error values. The text does not report uncertainty for the depth results or describe a control for that comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The AUC/logloss performance comparisons in Table 1, Table 2, Figure 5, and Table 3 do not report training classification error or another measure named by the claim versions, so they were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and size or regularization conditions.
Gradient-descent outcomes and extra-width effects in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, its prevention by identity residual shortcuts, longer-training controls, and special-initialization or Fixup conditions.
Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth, including matched-variance Gaussian versus orthogonal weights.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Different architecture and outcome measures are reasons these results fit no listed version; they are not evidence limiting V3's scope. The study's references to initialization, batch normalization, and Fixup do not supply direct tests of V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Identity residual shortcuts, batch-normalized convolutional networks, ImageNet, CIFAR-10, longer-training error comparisons, and the Fixup and special-initialization conditions.
Initialization comparisons and signal or gradient propagation across depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature or sharpness, squared loss, and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization comparisons, training-speed and learning-rate tolerance measures, and Fixup conditions.

rows.subject: vanilla DNN
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated training stability across network depths from 1 to 100 layers.
rows.value: The training process of vanilla DNNs completely collapses at depth 27.
rows.note: The paper states the collapse depth, but gives no training classification-error value.
rows.check: The collapse at depth 27 is reported correctly, but does not measure V3's training-error degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks. Section 4.1.1 specifies that reported metrics are on the test set; Figure 5 reports AUC/logloss across depths.

rows.subject: DNN w/ SML
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated training stability across network depths from 1 to 100 layers with Skip Meta Logit.
rows.value: SML can stably train networks up to depth 100.
rows.note: SML uses Skip Logit and Meta Tanh; it is not the identity residual shortcut condition in V3. No training classification-error value is reported.
rows.check: Stable training through depth 100 is the authors' reported interpretation, but SML combines logit-level skips with Meta Tanh rather than identity residual shortcuts. Test-set AUC/logloss cannot establish V3's training-error result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Criteo DNNs with SML, tested from 1 to 100 layers
reader_labels.reason: SML training remained stable up to depth 100, while vanilla DNN training collapsed at depth 27, but SML is a different shortcut design and the paper gives no training-error values (R1, R2).
